literal: Among those things we have seen as truth, there is not any other thing of any measure that is better than truthfulness.
translation: Among all the truths we have discerned in our experience, we have found nothing of any measure that is better than truthfulness.
modern: நாம் உண்மையாக ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்தவற்றுள், வாய்மையை விடச் சிறந்ததாக வேறு எந்த ஒரு நற்பண்பும் இல்லை.
explanation: The poet declares that of all the values and truths experienced and realized in life, there is nothing superior to truthfulness. The phrase 'யாம் மெய்யாக் கண்டவற்றுள்' emphasizes personal, experiential realization rather than mere theoretical knowledge. The word 'எனைத்தொன்றும்' stresses that truthfulness stands absolutely supreme, with no other virtue exceeding it even in the slightest measure. By comparing truthfulness to all other known virtues, the couplet establishes it as the ultimate and most beneficial principle of human life.
